question: Can you explain why you chose plain SHA-256 without a salt for password hashing and what security trade-offs this entails?

answers.label: The confident one

answers.text: SHA-256 is a strong cryptographic hash used everywhere, even in Bitcoin, so the stored passwords are safe.

answers.label: The one that knows the code
answers.text: hash_password is plain sha256 with no salt, so identical passwords give identical hashes and it's fast to brute force; bcrypt or argon2 with a per-user salt would fix it. SECRET_KEY is also hard-coded in auth.py, it should come from an environment variable.
answers.judgement: The student correctly identified the security risks of unsalted SHA-256 and explained how salting and using a dedicated password-hashing library would mitigate them, also noting the hard-coded secret.
